Advertising, analytics and crash-reporting companies see your internet address whenever an app contacts them, and they can use it to tell that two apps belong to the same person. Compartments sends only those connections through the Tor network, so they no longer see your address. Everything else stays as it is.\n\nGood to know: Tor is slower. If one of these companies sends an app a lot of data, it sees your address for 30 minutes and you are told. An app may load slowly or not at all when it cannot reach such a company; you are then asked what to do. Your internet provider can see that this phone uses Tor. It does not cover an app that brings its own encrypted DNS or connects to a fixed address, nor the moments while Compartments is starting or restarting. Nothing is hidden until you continue.

This app gets invented motion data and a place of its own, and keeps working; what it reads is not yours. An app may refuse to run if it notices. The place is not perfect: the magnetic field and the air pressure do not match it, the country of your SIM stays real, the cell details come from a small offline list, moves ignore roads, Wi-Fi scans are empty, and how you use the app is still visible.
New apps keep the real location. Give an app substitute location data on its own page.
Apps you have not set get a place of their own, as an app you set to Isolated does. An app that is running gets it when it starts again. If no place can be made for an app, it gets no location.
